sentences.text: Researchers developed a computational sensor that detects glutamate by converting its binding into an electrical signal without enzymes, utilizing a polydopamine recognition layer and a Prussian Blue transducer on a carbon fiber electrode.

This device operates linearly for glutamate concentrations between 0.10 and 400 micromolar, detecting levels as low as 31 nanomolar while showing that other substances caused less than 14% of the response seen with 10 micromolar glutamate and resisting protein buildup during consistent readings.
The sensor successfully tracked changing levels of glutamate release in a gel mimicking a brain hematoma, leading the authors to conclude it functions effectively in this specific model.
